description: Load an exported design into this graph. THE DOCUMENT SHAPE: {"nodes":[{"node_type":"Requirement","node_id":"req:x","properties":{...}}],"edges":[{"edge_type":"SATISFIES","from_id":"cap:x","to_id":"req:x","properties":{}}]}. Only `nodes` is required: `graph_id`, `stamp`, both hashes and `edges` are OPTIONAL. Endpoint types come from the document's nodes or this graph; describe_schema lists each node_type's properties. EACH NODE IS STATED WHOLE: a node already here is replaced, so a property the document leaves out is removed (counted in `properties_removed` / `properties_changed`). A node is refused only when it lacks a required property. To EDIT existing nodes, pass `merge: true` (what the document omits is kept) or use create_nodes. Anything not in the document is left alone. Atomic: a document that fails validation leaves the graph untouched, and EVERY invalid item is reported at once; an edge whose endpoint is missing is reported, not dropped. IDENTITY: an EMPTY store adopts the document's `graph_id` (`adopted_identity`); any other keeps its name. A document from a NEWER reflow2 is REFUSED unless `accept_newer`: this binary would write its defaults onto it. `materialized` names every Type.property written and not stated. OPTIONS: `check_only` runs it all and WRITES NOTHING; `add_only` REFUSES what the design already holds; `proposals_only` REFUSES what settles or approves. Ask for this when you want to load a design or model file that someone exported or sent you.

accept_newer.description:
Import a document stamped by a NEWER reflow2 than this server anyway.
Default false: such an import is REFUSED, because this binary would
write its own schema defaults onto every record the newer reflow2 left
implicit (853 AUTHORED_BY edges gained `role: author` that way on
2026-09-14) and nothing in the result would say so. Pass true only when
you mean to read it with this binary — the report's `materialized` field
then names exactly what was written that the document did not state.

add_only.description:
ADD ONLY. Default false. true: a node whose id the design already
holds, under any type, is REFUSED, and so is an edge it already holds
(same type, same two ends); each is listed with every other fault and
nothing is written. New nodes are written, and so is a new edge between
nodes the design holds, or between one it holds and a new one.

check_only.description:
CHECK the document and WRITE NOTHING. Default false. true: the whole
import runs exactly as a real one would, with every other option as
given, and is then discarded whether or not it had faults. The design,
its identity and its committed export are left exactly as they were.
The reply says so (`checked_only: true`, `written: false`, a `note`)
and carries `would_be_refused`, `faults` (every item the same import
would be refused for, the same lines a refused import lists) and
`would_write` (the counts it would write). A check that finds faults is a normal
reply, not an error.

document.description:
A document previously returned by `export_graph`. Omit when passing
`path`.

echo.description: What the reply carries. `receipt` (the default) names the node, echoes each stored value of at most 200 characters, gives longer ones by size, and names the snapshot that keeps anything a revise replaced. `node` returns the whole stored node and every prior value.

merge.description:
Keep what a partial node leaves out. Default false: the document states
each node WHOLE, so a property a node already holds and the document
omits is removed (a round trip reproduces the design; a document can
drop a property), and the reply counts it in `properties_removed`.
true: each node the design already holds takes the document's
properties and keeps every other one it has, as create_nodes does. A
node not yet in the design is written as stated either way.

path.description:
Read the document from this file instead — the committed design export,
usually. Prefer this to inlining: it avoids carrying a large document
through the conversation, and it records that this seat is now in step
with that file, which is what clears a `req:stale-seat-knows` refusal.

proposals_only.description:
PROPOSALS ONLY. Default false. true: the document may propose and may
not settle. REFUSED, each listed with every other fault: a node that
would arrive settled (an accepted requirement or decision, a rule with
`enforced` stated, an increment closed without arriving); a node the
design holds whose settling property the document would change at all,
back out of a settled value included; an AUTHORED_BY edge it would
create or change that carries the `approver` role. Judged on what would
be stored, after `merge` and the schema's defaults.

name: import_graph
title: Import a Design
